itemRankNote: Proposed, not yet confirmed by review. Decision 4. With the young cap of five sourced questions spent across every group the child tapped, a head-only 6-year-old receives items 1, 3, 2, 5 and 4 and nothing else, so this ordering decides what a child is actually asked. Light leads because it is the only item both literatures support independently (ICHD-3 criterion D and RCH's 'Signs of meningism (photophobia, neck stiffness)'), because source 12 supplies validated child wording for it, and because it is the question `FOLLOW_UPS.head` already ships -- ranking it below the cutoff would be a visible regression. Item 12 added 2026-09-08 at the user's request, RANKED LAST and deliberately so. The packet argued against proposing it because ICHD-3 says unilateral pain "usually emerges in late adolescence", so laterality does not discriminate migraine from tension-type at 4-12. That argument stands and is why it is last. It is included anyway on this project's existing principle -- established for the head-injury fall-height thresholds -- that the app captures the raw fact and lets the nurse classify. The asymmetry worth knowing: tension-type is bilateral BY DEFINITION, so "one side" points toward migraine, while "both sides" discriminates nothing. It is a one-directional test. REORDERED 2026-09-08 by iris, who chose the top six directly: 1, 3, 2, 12, 8, 6. Six because that is the 8+ cap; under-8s get the first five. This promotes item 8 (worse on coughing/sneezing/bending, the classic raised-ICP sign) from 7th, where it never shipped, and item 12 (laterality) from 10th. It drops item 5 (blurry) and item 4 (worse on movement) out of the shipped set -- see the cost note below. The earlier ordering was "Proposed, not yet confirmed by review"; this one is the review.

minAgeNotes.*: JUDGEMENT, NOT A CITATION. No item in this packet carries an age floor, and the empty object is a decision rather than an omission. Two floors were considered and rejected. (1) A CAPABILITY floor of 6 on items 1 and 6, from ICHD-3's 'In young children, photophobia and phonophobia may be inferred from their behaviour' -- rejected because ICHD-3 gives no age for 'young children', so any number would be invented, and because it would strip 4- and 5-year-olds of the only follow-up question group `head` currently ships. Handled instead by decision 6, a WORDING rule: the young-tier wording of items 1 and 6 must name a thing the child could not do (source 10's 'inability to watch TV or play on the computer or on electronic games'), not a judgement about light or sound. (2) A VALIDITY floor of 7 across the characterisation items, from source 12 (Kellier et al.) enrolling ages 7-17 -- rejected under brief section 4, because those same items are plain history in NICE NG127 section 1.21, which is written for children UNDER 12 and sets no floor at all. A validity floor on an item that is also plain history in a complaint guideline setting no floor is an invention, not a citation.

British and Australian idiom, banned project-wide and re-banned here because EVERY guideline source in this packet is British or Australian -- RCH writes 'haemorrhage' and 'paracetamol', NICE writes 'unwell', HeadSmart writes 'fits'. Decision 1 rules 'do you have'
preferredNote: No wording preferences can be expressed yet -- this packet has no candidates. Stage 2 must honour decision 6, which is a wording rule and not an age floor: the YOUNG-tier wording of items 1 and 6 must name a thing the child could not do (source 10, Table 2: 'Sensitivity to light and sounds as indicated by inability to watch TV or play on the computer or on electronic games'), because ICHD-3 states that 'In young children, photophobia and phonophobia may be inferred from their behaviour'. The OLDER tier may ask about the sensation directly, in Kellier 2023's words ('Has light bothered you today?', 'Has sound bothered you today?').
factsNote: JUDGEMENT, NOT A CITATION -- no source assigns facts; the reasoning is the bank's dedupe behaviour in `keyOf` and `bankQuestions`. REUSED: `light-hurts` (decision 8 -- it is the id of the head group's hand-written FOLLOW_UPS entry and the fact eyes/complaint item 5 and tummy/vomiting item 4 already carry; `bright-light-hurts` in skin/rash names the same clinical fact but is unreachable from here because skin/rash is depth `surface`, and merging the two slugs is a bank-wide change flagged for review); `vomiting`; `blurry` (eyes/complaint item 4 -- reused as a slug, but this packet proposes its own item because eyes/complaint serves group `eyes` only); `stopping-normal-things` (back/pain item 12, region-neutral by construction). COINED: `morning-headache` (decision 7 -- NOT `morning-vomiting`, which establishes when the THROWING UP happens; the raised-ICP red flag needs both halves and sharing the slug would let one suppress the other. Also not `morning-pain`, which is limb/pain's and is region-neutral in wording); `sound-hurts` (nothing in the bank names sound sensitivity; `hard-to-hear` is hearing LOSS and the opposite finding); `head-worse-moving` (the bank already has three region-specific slugs for this same trigger -- `worse-on-exertion`, `worse-on-movement`, `worse-when-playing` -- and following the precedent stops a head answer and a leg answer collapsing into one). UNTAGGED: item 7, matching head-injury item 2, limb-injury item 4 and tummy/acute-pain item 7, because this project keeps region-specific trajectory questions separate by leaving them without a fact.
gateNote: Group `head` asks the MECHANISM gate first and the DEPTH gate second, and only asks depth when mechanism is `no-injury` or `unknown` (GROUP_GATE.head). This packet serves `no-injury` + `inside`; `head-injury` serves `injury`. They never coexist, which is why both carry packetRank 50 -- the rank only ever competes with `general-unwell` (rank 50, cross-cutting, and exhausted after the home-group packet) inside group `head`. `skin-rash` is depth `surface` and therefore cannot reach a child served by this packet, which is why no rash or skin criterion is carried here. KNOWN GATE FAILURE, in Still open: a child whose headache began three days after a fall may answer 'it just started hurting' and be routed here, where NG127's 'headache occurring within 5 days of a head injury' is asked by neither packet.
itemRankCost: Items 5 and 4 no longer reach a child in a head-only report. Item 5 (blurry) is the child-reportable half of the strongest single predictor in the only prediction study located (Manoyana, ocular findings OR 19.9) -- but that study is 109 children, retrospective, 47% lesion-positive, and its examination findings are the nurse's half anyway. Item 4 (aggravation by activity) is an ICHD-3 C-criterion, but the sensation screen and the intensity screen already carry two of the other three, so migraine characterisation is not lost entirely. Both remain accepted and ranked, and ship the moment the cap grows.
